problem: Find out whether managers affect results and what good ones do.
title: Google studies what makes a good manager and trains managers on the findings
context: Google had questioned whether managers mattered and decided to test it with data.
decision_made: Analyse performance reviews, surveys and manager awards for more than 10,000 observations, then build training on the habits found.
action_taken: Published a list of manager behaviours, first eight and later ten, with coaching and not micromanaging among them.
observed_outcome: Google's HR chief said 75 percent of the worst-performing managers improved significantly. One source reported the average manager score rising from 83 to 88 percent between 2010 and 2012.
lessons: Looking at internal data can test strong beliefs about management and give concrete training targets.
limitations: Results are reported by the company and its HR leader. The number of habits varies by source, and a "favorability" metric was not found in this form.

claims.claim_text: Google began Project Oxygen in 2008, analysing over 10,000 manager observations to identify what makes a great manager.
Laszlo Bock said 75 percent of Google's worst-performing managers improved significantly.
